# testdata — Codec 8E frames

These `*.hex` files are AVL packets used by the table-driven parser tests
(`internal/protocol/testdata_test.go`). Each file is a single hex-encoded
Codec 8 Extended (`0x8E`) frame:

```
[4B zero preamble][4B data length][0x8E][record count][records...][record count][4B CRC16]
```

## Status: SYNTHETIC (pre-bench)

The frames here today are **synthetic but structurally valid** — generated by
this gateway's own `protocol.BuildAVL` encoder, so they exercise the full
parse + CRC path. They are NOT captures from real hardware yet.

During the bench phase, replace/augment these with **real captured frames** from
an FMB930 (raw TCP capture of the bytes after the IMEI handshake). Drop each
capture in as `something.hex` and the existing test will pick it up
automatically. Keep the synthetic ones too — they pin known field values.

## Current files

| File | Records | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `telemetry_single.hex` | 1 | Stationary, ignition on, DOUTs low, ext≈39.5 V |
| `telemetry_moving.hex`  | 1 | Moving 27 km/h, DOUT1 high (unlocked), odometer present |
| `telemetry_multi.hex`   | 2 | Multi-record packet; second record shows movement onset |

IO ids used in these frames mirror the FMB930 AVL id constants in
`internal/adapter/fmb930.go` (239 ignition, 240 movement, 66/67 voltages,
21 GSM, 179/180 DOUT1/DOUT2, 16 odometer). Several of those ids are still
`TODO(verify wiki)` — see the top-level `README.md`.

## Regenerating

The synthetic frames were produced with a throwaway `main` that calls
`protocol.BuildAVL(...)` and hex-encodes the result. Any Go program in the
module can import `internal/protocol` to rebuild them; there is no committed
generator (kept out of the build surface on purpose).
